subject.title: [Feature]: Import real Chrome-family profile cookies into the managed browser

question: Should agents be allowed to copy authenticated system-browser cookies into persistent managed profiles, and what affirmative consent and default should govern that transfer?
rationale: Code review can verify cryptography and routing, but only maintainers can authorize this new authentication-state boundary and decide whether Keychain consent is sufficient for agent-initiated imports.

options.title: Opt-in with per-import approval
options.body: Disable the feature by default and require a human-visible approval showing browser, source profile, destination profile, and domain scope for every import.

options.title: Enable with Keychain consent
options.body: Accept the proposed default-on behavior and treat the macOS Keychain prompt plus domain filtering as sufficient operator control.

options.title: Reject persistent import
options.body: Keep authenticated access limited to live attach or extension-relay paths so OpenClaw does not persist copied browser credentials.

recommendation.title: Opt-in with per-import approval
recommendation.body: Disable the feature by default and require a human-visible approval showing browser, source profile, destination profile, and domain scope for every import.

likelyOwner.reason: He established the browser plugin boundary and introduced the current existing-session path, making him the strongest history-backed owner for the product and security choice.
